what.text: Setmelanotide is an injected peptide that switches on the melanocortin 4 (MC4) receptor in the brain, which helps control hunger, fullness and energy use. It is sold as Imcivree by Rhythm Pharmaceuticals and injected under the skin once a day.

It is approved only for rare kinds of obesity: obesity caused by certain gene changes (POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency), Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS), and acquired hypothalamic obesity, which follows damage to the brain’s hypothalamus, for example from a tumor. The label says it is not approved for common (polygenic) obesity and would not be expected to help there.
It also acts weakly on the MC1 receptor in skin pigment cells, which is why it darkens the skin in many people.

research.text: Setmelanotide has been tested in small trials, because the conditions it treats are rare. The trials were paid for by Rhythm Pharmaceuticals. They are listed below as they were run.

research.title: POMC and LEPR deficiency (two Phase 3 trials)

facts.v: single-arm, open-label, with a short blinded placebo withdrawal period
10 people with POMC deficiency and 11 with LEPR deficiency, aged 6 and older
share losing at least 10% of body weight; hunger scores

research.found: 8 of 10 people (80%) with POMC deficiency and 5 of 11 (45%) with LEPR deficiency lost at least 10% of their weight. Hunger scores fell. Injection-site reactions and skin darkening were the most common side effects. There was no placebo group for the full year. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02896192 and NCT03287960.

src.label: Clément et al., POMC and LEPR phase 3 trials, Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol

research.title: Bardet-Biedl and Alström syndromes

facts.v: Phase 3: 14 weeks randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, then 52 weeks open-label
38 people aged 6 and older with obesity and BBS (32) or Alström syndrome (6)
daily setmelanotide up to 3.0 mg or placebo, then setmelanotide for all
share of people 12 and older with BBS losing at least 10% of weight after 52 weeks of setmelanotide

research.found: 32.3% of people 12 and older with BBS lost at least 10% of their weight. For Alström syndrome, the findings were inconclusive. Skin darkening (61%) and injection-site redness (48%) were the most common side effects. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03746522.

src.label: Haqq et al., Bardet-Biedl and Alström phase 3, Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol

research.title: TRANSCEND: acquired hypothalamic obesity

facts.v: 120 people aged 4 to 66 with obesity after a hypothalamic tumor, lesion or injury
daily setmelanotide 1.5 to 3.0 mg or placebo
percent change in BMI; hunger score

research.found: BMI changed by -16.5% on setmelanotide and +3.3% on placebo. Hunger scores fell more on setmelanotide. Serious side effects happened in 28% on setmelanotide and 8% on placebo. Skin darkening, nausea, vomiting and headache were the most common. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05774756.

src.label: Miller et al., TRANSCEND, N Engl J Med

research.text: The FDA label describes the hypothalamic obesity trial with 142 patients analyzed, a larger group than the 120 in the journal report.

us.text: Setmelanotide is FDA approved as Imcivree, first in November 2020, for three rare kinds of obesity. It is not approved for common obesity. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: approved to reduce excess weight and keep it off in people 2 and older with obesity from POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency confirmed by a gene test, or from Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and in people 4 and older with acquired hypothalamic obesity.
Drugs@FDA lists efficacy supplements approved in 2022, 2024 and March 2026; the current label adds BBS and acquired hypothalamic obesity to the first gene-based uses.
the label says it is not approved for common (polygenic) obesity or other genetic syndromes. Any such use is off-label, and the label says it would not be expected to help.
compounded drugs are not FDA approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

src.label: FDA, Compounding and the FDA: Q&A

us.text: Imcivree is approved only for rare, specific causes of obesity. It is not approved for common obesity.

world.lead: Setmelanotide is approved in the US, the EU and Canada, and has a UK marketing authorisation, for rare genetic and hypothalamic obesity. It is not named on WADA’s list.

countries.status: Approved medicine (Imcivree) for obesity from POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency, Bardet-Biedl syndrome, or acquired hypothalamic obesity. Prescription-only.
Authorised medicine (Imcivree, 2021), an orphan medicine, for POMC/PCSK1/LEPR deficiency and Bardet-Biedl syndrome. The current EU indication also covers acquired hypothalamic obesity.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Setmelanotide is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or the 2027 Monitoring Program. Because it is approved, the List’s S0 class for unapproved drugs does not apply.

side.text: The Imcivree label has no boxed warning. It warns about sexual side effects, depression, serious allergy and skin darkening, and about hormone and salt problems in people with hypothalamic obesity.

items.text: spontaneous erections and more frequent erections happened in trials. The label says an erection lasting more than 4 hours needs emergency care. Women had sexual side effects too.
have occurred. The label advises watching for new or worse depression.
most people in trials had darker skin, which reverses after stopping. Existing moles can darken and new ones can appear; the label calls for full skin checks before and during treatment.
anaphylaxis has been reported, usually within minutes to hours of an injection.
serious events of acute adrenal insufficiency were reported in 5% on Imcivree and none on placebo. In people who also had central diabetes insipidus, low and high blood sodium were reported.

items.lead: Most common (20% or more in at least one use):
items.text: skin darkening, injection-site reactions, nausea, headache, diarrhea, belly pain, vomiting, depression and spontaneous penile erection.
the label says to stop Imcivree when pregnancy is recognized unless the benefit outweighs the risk to the fetus.

unconfirmed: The UK status comes from NICE guidance, not an MHRA record; whether the UK authorisation now covers Bardet-Biedl syndrome or hypothalamic obesity was not checked.
Which specific use each 2022, 2024 and 2026 FDA supplement added was not confirmed from FDA approval letters.
Australia’s ARTG was not searched directly; only TGA’s product information database was.
surprises: Setmelanotide’s US label says it is approved only for rare causes of obesity and would not be expected to help in common obesity.
